sara_support: FYI — ACME (ticket #12345) reported a mobile dev accidentally committed a webhook/API key in a public repo. They found it in a paste and want immediate rotation + an audit export for compliance. They pasted a partial key: ri_live_abc123... Can security confirm retention window and whether we can prove usage?

devon_infra: copied. Do we have the full key id? We can revoke immediately but need to confirm it wasn't a short-lived client token. Also, customer provided a few request timestamps — any way to map those in audit logs quickly?

sara_support: They provided two request timestamps: 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z and 2026-03-15T14:12:28Z. Only partial key shown in repo. They say the mobile repo is public for ~3 hours.

lena_security: Prioritize rotation. For hosted accounts our default audit log retention is 90 days (longer on Dedicated/Enterprise with retention add-on). We can export request-level events for that key if we have the key id or can match by partial prefix and timestamps. Note: we do NOT have access to customer-managed KMS plaintext; for hosted keys we use Redwood-managed KMS — we can revoke API keys but cannot rotate customer-side embedded secrets in their mobile app. Recommend immediate key revoke + create new server-side key and advise moving to proxying through backend.

sara_support: Customer asked specifically: (1) can you prove the key was used only at those two times, (2) can you produce an audit CSV for regulators, (3) can we delete the key from your KMS completely?

kms-bot: Automated audit search complete. Matched 2 request events for prefix ri_live_abc123 (redacted). Events: 
- evt_20260315_141203 id=log-AB12 src_ip=198.51.100.23 path=/v1/embeddings model=text-embedding-3
- evt_20260315_141228 id=log-AB13 src_ip=198.51.100.23 path=/v1/chat/completions model=gpt-4o-mini
Export ready at s3://redwood-incident-exports/12345/2026-03-15-audit.csv (expires in 7 days).

lena_security: kms-bot — thanks. That aligns. On deletion: we cannot "delete" key material from our KMS if it's the primary key backing active API credentials without revoking the credential objects first. Process: (a) create new API key, (b) update customer to use new key, (c) revoke old key (status=revoked) which breaks issuance; we can then schedule key material destruction per KMS policy for hosted keys, but note customers on Private w/ customer-managed keys must handle their own KMS key lifecycle.

aaron_platform: Rotation playbook (short):
1) Console -> API Keys -> Create new key (name: "acme-mobile-rotation-2026-03-15")
2) Update any server-side services to use new key (do NOT put key in mobile)
3) Revoke old key via API: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/ri_live_abc123/revoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```
4) Confirm no further usage in audit logs (watch for 15 mins)
5) Attach exported CSV and incident ticket to customer response.

devon_infra: I'll open an internal incident (INC-2026-457) and run the revoke now. Will also snapshot the exported CSV to the incident ticket and upload to the s3 path provided. I'll take IP indicators for abuse team.

sara_support: Drafting reply to ACME: apology, confirm we will rotate + provide audit csv + recommend moving keys off-device and using server-side proxy + offer 90-day export and discuss extended retention options. Will include next steps and ETA.

lena_security: Also advise them to rotate any downstream secrets and check their git history for other exposures (use BFG or git-filter-repo). Offer a short guidance snippet for mobile: do not embed secrets; use ephemeral tokens minted by backend via OAuth or signed JWTs.

aaron_platform: One more note for support docs: add a small snippet in the rotation guide for customers showing how to revoke via API and how to request an audit export (support@redwood.ai with ticket id). I'll update the KB after this incident.

devon_infra: Revoke done. Old key status -> revoked. Monitoring audit log for any post-revoke calls (15m window). Uploaded export to INC-2026-457 and shared s3 link with legal/compliance.

kms-bot: Post-revoke scan: no additional successful uses found after 2026-03-15T14:12:28Z.

sara_support: Sent response to ACME with CSV link and rotation confirmation. They asked about longer retention — I offered to escalate to sales for an enterprise retention add-on.

lena_security: :thumbsup: Good runbook. Follow-up: recommend enabling organization-level rotation cadence and add mobile app secret best-practices to onboarding. Close when customer acknowledges and confirms rotated in their app/backends.

sara_support: Closing thread from support side once ACME confirms. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.
